pr_title: drivers: can: calculate a default SJW value if none is specified
pr_body:
Change the CAN timing API to automatically calculate a default (Re-)Synchronization Jump Width (SJW) value if none is set by the caller. This allows automatically scaling the SJW according to the number of Time Quanta (TQ) used for phase segment 2 instead of relying on a compile-time fallback value defined in devicetree.

Update the CAN controller drivers to solely use the `sjw` and `sjw-data` devicetree properties for setting the initial timing when devicetree timing parameters are specified in Time Quanta (TQ). Any timing set via the CAN timing APIs will contain either user-provided or automatically calculated SJW values. This includes any timing parameters calculated from `bus-speed` and `bus-speed-data` devicetree properties.
    
Update the CAN controller driver tests accordingly and remove the `CAN_SJW_NO_CHANGE` definition as it has lost its meaning.

Update the descriptions for the various CAN devicetree timing properties specified in Time Quanta (TQ) to make it clear that these, if present, are only used for the initial timing parameters. Deprecate the (Re-)Synchronization Jump Width (SJW) devicetree properties for both arbitration and data phase timing as these are now only used in combination with the other TQ-based CAN timing properties, which are all deprecated.

Fixes: #63033

The SJW needs to be a percentage of the nominal bit time. It has to be less than or equal to both PHASE_SEG1 and PHASE_SEG2 and must be within the range of the supported SJW values for the given controller. The default value `PHASE_SEG2 / 2` may be arbitrary, but it has precedence in other implementations (e.g. the Linux kernel), which is sufficient reason for going with this as default. The user/application is still free to overwrite any default calculated SJW with whatever calculation or default value they may choose.

Thank you for the review comments, all. Based on the comment, I have tried to simplify the API even further.

I have updated this patch set to reduce the `can_set_timing()` and `can_set_timing_data()` API functions to mere setters with built-in validation of the supplied timing parameters. They no longer attempt to calculate a default SJW in case none was specified, nor do they attempt to restore a default SJW value set in devicetree. They act as setters, no more, no less.

The calculation of a default, suitable SJW has been kept in the `can_calc_timing()` and `can_calc_timing_data()` API functions. These are also used by `can_set_bitrate()`/`can_set_bitrate_data()` and thus these functions will also calculate a default SJW. The calculation is still based on `PHASE_SEG2 / 2` as this has precedence in other implementations (e.g. the Linux kernel).

issue_context.title: RFC: drivers: can: fallback to default SJW set in devicetree is insufficient and causes communication errors
issue_context.body:
**Introduction**

In its most low-level form, CAN timing is configured in Time Quanta (TQ), where one TQ equals one CAN clock period (divided by the CAN clock prescaler, if any).

The nominal bit time can be calculated as `1 / bitrate` and each bit can be thought of as being divided into multiple segments. The length of these segments is expressed in TQ and determines the location of the sample point for the bit as seen in the following figure (copied from the CAN 2.0b specification):

![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/1076226/5eb59b4c-12c0-44e2-ad27-643242f7888a)

To accommodate different tolerances and clock skew in the CAN clock across nodes on the same CAN bus, the CAN controller must be able to resynchronize to the bitstream by either lengthening `PHASE_SEG1` or shortining `PHASE_SEG2`. The maximum allowed TQs for lengthening/shortening is controlled by an additional (Re-)Synchronization Jump Width (SJW) timing parameter.

In classical CAN 2.0b (and especially in older CAN controller implementations) the SJW is limited to a value from 1 to 4 TQ. In CAN-FD (and in some newer CAN controllers), this limitation is not present.

***Problem description***
The Zephyr CAN drivers rely on having a default SJW - and a separate, default SJW for the CAN-FD data phase - for a given CAN controller instance stored in the devicetree using the `sjw` and `sjw-data` properties.

This compile-time encoded SJW is used for _any_ bitrate later set via e.g. `can_set_bitrate()`/`can_set_bitrate_data()`. It is also used if the caller sets the `sjw` field to `CAN_SJW_NO_CHANGE` when calling `can_calc_timing()`/`can_calc_timing_data()`, although the latter two API calls does allow the caller to supply a custom SJW.

However, using the same compile-time encoded SJW for any bitrate is insufficient as this provides no way of scaling the tolerance along with the applied timing, resulting in either too tight resynchronization especially at higher bitrates or too loose resynchronization at lower bitrates.

**Proposed changes**
* The SJW specificed in the devicetree should only be used for _initial_ CAN timing configuration and _only_ if the remaining timing parameters are expressed in TQs (and not by specifying the sample point in per mille). 
* The `can_set_bitrate()`/`can_set_bitrate_data()` API calls should automatically calculate and set a suitable SJW based on the resulting timing parameters.
* The `can_calc_timing()`/`can_calc_timing_data()` API calls should calculate a suitable SJW _only_ if the caller did not supply an SJW (i.e. if the SJW field was set to `0`).

**Impact**
The current behaviour leads to communication errors, especially at higher bitrates, due to failing resynchronization.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA: c1ad82e5fbce7b8f24091d5e64a2f90d13bc1531

**Additional context**
I have looked into what other CAN stacks do when it comes to SJW settings. Some vendors set the SJW to the full length of `PHASE_SEG2` (which seems a bit extreme), others set it to half the length of `PHASE_SEG2`.

The Linux kernel was recently (September 2022) updated to use `PHASE_SEG2 / 2` for SJW unless userspace provided a custom SJW (see commit https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=80bcf5ec9927f0a8056495d746b74f57b1e1ad8b and https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/latest/source/drivers/net/can/dev/bittiming.c#L9).

**Detailed RFC**
Please see PR #63034.

**Dependencies**
None.

**Concerns and Unresolved Questions**
None.

**Alternatives**
Continue to have users/applications always calculate a suitable SJW themselves (which will lead the code for handling `CAN_SJW_NO_CHANGE` pretty much unused for any advanced usage scenario).
comments: A reference to a similar issue being reported in the Linux kernel: https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-can/msg08820.html This lead to the change in behaviour regarding SJW calculation in the Linux kernel as referenced above.
